newsitem.title: UK: Fidelity hires former London Exchange executive.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity hires former London Exchange executive.

text.p: Fidelity Brokerage Services, the European broking arm of the U.S. fund management giant, said on Wednesday it had hired former London Stock Exchange executive Giles Vardey as president and chief executive officer.

Vardey, 41, who departed from the Exchange in March after working there for seven years, will take up his new position in mid June. He succeeds Kenneth Rathgeber, acting president since November, who will return to the United States.
"We are very fortunate to have such an able executive join us," said Sherif Nada, president of Fidelity Brokerage Group.
"With his broad experience in the European securities industry, coupled with his visibility in the local market, Giles Vardey is uniquely suited to help us move our UK brokerage business forward."
In his position of director of markets development and marketing at the Exchange, Vardey was credited with playing a leading role in developing its new trading services.
The Exchange plans to introduce a computerised or "order-driven" market in October, replacing the current system where dealers or market-makers quote prices on screen and agree share trades by phone.
No reason was given for his departure, though the Exchange said at the time he was expected to resume his career in the securities industry.

Prior to joining the exchange, Vardey -- who gained an MA in politics, philosophy and economics from Balliol College, Oxford -- had been managing director and head of Swiss Bank Corp's equities group.
He had previously worked for Salomon Brothers and NatWest Securities.
Vardey was not immediately available for comment on his new appointment.
